title: Holbein stitch
subtitle: A double-running stitch that looks identical on both sides of the fabric
excerpt: Holbein stitch produces a solid running-stitch line that is reversible: the front and back look identical. It works in two passes, filling gaps on the return journey. It is the foundation stitch of blackwork embroidery.
sourceNotes: Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Holbein stitch entry. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), double running stitch section (Project Gutenberg #20776).

content.text: Holbein stitch uses a double running technique: the first pass lays alternating stitches and spaces along the line. The return pass fills the spaces exactly. Completing the solid line. The thread on the reverse mirrors the front.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 1 strand for fine work, 2 strands for bolder

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Evenweave linen or Aida for counted work; any fabric for freestyle

content.text: Work evenly spaced running stitches along the line, leaving gaps equal to each stitch length.
At the end of the line. Turn and work back, filling each gap with a stitch of exactly the same length.
The return stitches share the same holes as the end points of the outward stitches.
Keep both the stitch length and the gap length identical throughout both passes.

items.fix: Count threads or use marked intervals. Every stitch and every gap must be the same length.
items.cause: Outward stitches and gaps are not equal length.
items.symptom: The return pass does not line up with the gaps

items.fix: Share the exact hole at each stitch end. The needle should enter the same hole the previous stitch exited.
items.cause: Stitches are overlapping rather than filling exact gaps.
items.symptom: The back of the fabric looks different from the front

content.text: Holbein stitch is the foundation of blackwork embroidery, where geometric patterns are built from reversible lines. The two-pass double
method is also used in counted thread work and Assisi embroidery.
